rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the opinion to preserve unanimity with a narrow Hudson/Ward intent-effects holding that MVRA restitution, imposed at sentencing and entered in the criminal judgment “in addition to any other penalty,” is punishment for Ex Post Facto purposes. Separate writings are most likely from Thomas or Gorsuch to emphasize original meaning/anti-evasion principles and from Alito to add Mendoza-Martinez effects analysis, while others may concur only to stress narrowness.
